label: GO step, late in episode (trial >= ~65), after a rewarded trial, when the policy picks a1
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1/D2), only when the previous trial was rewarded (in_rew at D1 = 1; 0 activations otherwise), only when the policy at this step prefers a1 (model_act == 1 carries 99.9% of mass; strongly a1 logit, choice > 8 holds 84% of mass), and only late in the episode: zero activity before ep_trial ~55, ramping from 60 to plateau by 80-99. The episode-time gating suggests a slow drift in the hidden state over the episode rather than a task variable. Does not depend on transition type or core pattern beyond these; does not fire on a2-choice GO steps or after unrewarded trials. Dev: P 0.77, R 0.95, F1 0.85, mass recall 0.99 (ep_trial >= 60 gives R 0.99, P 0.70). Uses only the agent own current policy output and observed reward; no future variables. Magnitude is small (max 0.022) and not further characterized.

issues: The factual claims hold on dev. Activity is only at GO (D1 and D2 have 0 of 380619 steps each). Only 45 of 33561 active steps have prev_reward==0. model_act==1 holds 0.999 of the mass and choice>8.07 holds 0.844. The activation rate is 0 for trials 0-49, 139 actives in trials 50-59, then 0.039, 0.073, 0.086 and 0.088 for the 60s to 90s, so it does level off. The original predicate reproduces on dev (P 0.773 R 0.948 F1 0.851) and on test (P 0.761 R 0.953 F1 0.846, mass recall 0.991).

The explanation is wrong that the late-episode dependence is 'a slow drift in the hidden state, not a task variable'. The agent's own value estimate fully replaces ep_trial. No active step has value >= 7.73 and almost none have value in [7.54, 7.73) (60 steps). On dev, GO & prev_reward==1 & model_act==1 & value<7.5 with no ep_trial term gets recall 0.994 and F1 0.82. Adding ep_trial>=55 on top of value<7.4 & choice>5 leaves the test scores unchanged (identical n_predicted, 37472), so the value condition already implies late episode. The simplest reading is that the unit is gated by a low value estimate, which falls as the episode nears its end. It is not best described as an unexplained time drift.

There is a systematic class of false positives: GO steps where the policy only weakly prefers a1. On test, many false-positive windows have good=S2 or recent switches, which are cases with a lower a1 logit. Adding choice>5 raises dev precision from 0.77 to 0.85 at almost no recall cost (0.948 to 0.926). Combined with value<7.4, test F1 rises from 0.846 to 0.891. The explanation reports the choice>8 mass share but leaves logit strength out of the predicate.
The missed activations are scattered and weak (test: 1564 steps holding 0.9% of the mass, all at near-zero activation). They are not a systematic class.
The 'no future variables' claim holds. value, choice and model_act are the agent's own outputs at that step.
skeptic.revised_label: GO step after a rewarded trial, when the policy strongly favours a1 and the agent's value estimate is low (which happens late in the episode, trial >= ~60)
